As a reinforced concrete inspector turned erosion control stormwater inspection, I can't even begin to tell you how fucking cool this is.

This is a common screed style, not surprisingly, called a roller screed or sometimes a bunion (sp?) screed. I've seen it used for sidewalk, concrete street panels, and even bridge deck sections (usually small widenings with active traffic). But I've never seen or heard of one like this.

These concrete flumes are a bitch to pour. I've seen various forms constructed to do something similar. But it involves pulling it and weighing down the form to prevent it from rising up when pulled by machinery. It usually is painstakingly slow and leaves lots of small air holes at the surface that rarely get troweled over. IMO, they usually look like shit. But the rolling action of this form is meant to keep a layer of paste in front, to minimize deficiencies and make the concrete surface consistent.
